WebSocket Connection Replay Attack [Spoofing, Tampering, CWE-294] on WebSocket API Gateway, Game Logic Lambda, Game State Cache: Without proper message authentication and sequencing, an attacker can capture WebSocket messages and replay them later to manipulate game state or impersonate other players An attacker captures game action messages (e.g., player movements or actions) and replays them to duplicate in-game actions or resources

Unauthorized API Access and Request Spoofing [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on REST API Gateway, WebSocket API Gateway, Game Logic Lambda: The API endpoints lack proper authentication and authorization mechanisms, allowing attackers to make direct API calls without valid credentials An attacker could craft API requests with spoofed player IDs to access or modify other players' game data

Game Server Instance Compromise [Tampering, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-20] on EC2 Game Servers, Auto Scaling Group, Security Groups: Lack of input validation and security hardening on EC2 instances could allow attackers to exploit game server vulnerabilities An attacker sends malformed game packets that exploit buffer overflows or other vulnerabilities in the game server software

Data Storage Security Vulnerabilities [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-311] on DynamoDB Table, ElastiCache Cluster, VPC Security Groups: Lack of encryption in transit and at rest could allow attackers to intercept or access sensitive game data An attacker performs MITM attack to capture unencrypted data between services, or gains access to unencrypted data at rest

Auto Scaling DoS Attack [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on Auto Scaling Group, EC2 Game Servers, CloudWatch Alarms: Attackers generate artificial load to trigger auto scaling beyond normal operational requirements Coordinated botnet attack generates massive traffic causing rapid scaling and excessive AWS costs

API Response Interception and Manipulation [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-319] on CloudFront Distribution, API Gateway, Game Logic Lambda: Without proper response signing and encryption, attackers can intercept and modify API responses before they reach the client Attacker uses a proxy to modify game state responses, manipulating scores or player positions
